items.title: PSMA-targeted Therapy and Androgen Suppression in Low-volume Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This trial tests whether adding Lu-177-PSMA-617 (a radioactive drug that targets prostate cancer cells) to standard hormone therapy improves outcomes in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer that has spread to only a few sites. Patients may receive hormone therapy alone or combined with the PSMA therapy and/or abiraterone. This is for newly diagnosed or recurrent metastatic disease with limited spread.

items.title: Tarlatamab Study for DLL3-positive Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates tarlatamab, a novel immunotherapy targeting the DLL3 protein, in patients with metastatic prostate cancer that has stopped responding to prior treatments. The study is currently recruiting patients whose cancer has progressed despite previous therapy and tests positive for the DLL3 marker.

items.title: ABBV-969 Safety and Efficacy Study in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial tests ABBV-969, an investigational drug, as a single treatment in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study evaluates different doses to determine safety and how the drug moves through the body, with plans to identify the best dose for future studies. Enrollment is no longer accepting new patients.

items.title: Immunotherapy Plus Cabozantinib for Rare Genitourinary Tumors
items.summary: This phase 2 trial combines cabozantinib (a targeted therapy) with two immunotherapy drugs (nivolumab and ipilimumab) for patients with rare genitourinary tumors including some prostate cancers. The study tests whether this three-drug combination works better than single agents for tumors with no other treatment options.

items.title: Low Dose Naltrexone for Fatigue in Prostate Cancer Patients
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies whether low-dose naltrexone can reduce fatigue in men with prostate cancer receiving hormone therapy (ADT). All participants are on standard androgen deprivation therapy, and some may also be taking newer hormone medicines. The study focuses on managing treatment side effects rather than treating the cancer itself.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel to Apalutamide for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether adding chemotherapy (docetaxel) improves outcomes in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer who haven't achieved a deep PSA response after initial treatment with apalutamide and hormone therapy. The study compares treatment intensification versus continuing current therapy in patients whose PSA levels remain elevated.

items.title: Abemaciclib With or Without Immunotherapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial tested whether abemaciclib (a targeted chemotherapy) alone or combined with atezolizumab (an immunotherapy) can shrink or slow the growth of metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study also evaluated the safety of combining these two drugs.

items.title: AMO959 Plus Lu-177-PSMA With Hormone Therapy in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial combines AMO959 with Lu-177-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy and hormone therapy in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have failed one prior hormone treatment. The study first tests safety and optimal dosing, then evaluates effectiveness in patients who haven't yet received chemotherapy.

items.title: AZD8359 STEAP2-Targeted Therapy First-in-Human Study for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study is the first to test AZD8359, a treatment targeting the STEAP2 protein on prostate cancer cells, in patients with metastatic disease. The study tests different doses and delivery methods to find the safest and most effective approach, then expands to test selected doses in larger patient groups.

items.title: Mevrometostat for Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer and Other Cancers
items.summary: This phase 1 study tests mevrometostat alone or with enzalutamide in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after prior treatments. The study is currently enrolling patients with mCRPC in Part 3, which includes both single-drug and combination treatment groups.

items.title: PSMA PET-Guided Radiation Plus Darolutamide in Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether adding stereotactic body radiation therapy (SBRT) to all visible tumors identified by advanced PSMA imaging improves outcomes when combined with darolutamide and hormone therapy. After 6 months of drug treatment, patients with remaining active tumors are randomized to continue medications with or without targeted radiation to each tumor site.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Combinations for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study evaluates ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, given alone or with other treatments in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to find safe doses that can be used in combination and to measure PSA levels and tolerability during treatment.

items.title: Cediranib Plus Olaparib Versus Olaparib Alone for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This randomized phase 2 trial compares olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) alone versus combined with cediranib (which blocks tumor blood vessel growth) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study tests whether the combination can better stop cancer growth by preventing DNA repair and reducing blood supply to tumors.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Versus Chemotherapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), a targeted antibody-drug conjugate, to standard chemotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study's main goal is to determine if patients treated with I-DXd live longer overall and have longer periods without cancer growth compared to those receiving chemotherapy.

items.title: PDS01ADC Plus Docetaxel and Abiraterone for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 study tests PDS01ADC, an antibody-drug conjugate, combined with docetaxel chemotherapy and abiraterone hormone therapy in men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, and with docetaxel alone in castration-resistant disease. The trial evaluates safety and whether these combinations can delay cancer progression.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 study tests whether combining mevrometostat (PF-06821497) with enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't previously received enzalutamide or abiraterone. This is a large confirmatory trial of the combination approach.

items.title: Adaptive Dosing Schedule for Lu-177-PSMA Therapy in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares different dosing schedules of lutetium Lu-177-PSMA (a radioactive treatment) to see if spacing out doses based on individual response can improve quality of life without reducing survival. The study is for patients with hormone-resistant prostate cancer that may have spread, and tests whether personalized timing of this PSMA-targeted treatment is better than the standard every-6-weeks schedule.

items.title: Cabozantinib Plus Lu-177-PSMA for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1b study tests escalating doses of cabozantinib combined with Lu-177-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial aims to identify safe dose combinations and evaluate preliminary effectiveness. Enrollment is currently suspended.

items.title: RO7656594 Safety and Activity Study in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 study evaluates the safety, how the drug moves through the body, and preliminary activity of RO7656594 in patients with advanced or metastatic prostate cancer. The trial will identify recommended doses for future studies of this investigational treatment.

items.title: Lu-177-PSMA Safety in Patients With Kidney Impairment
items.summary: This phase 2 study examines how kidney function affects the safety and distribution of lutetium Lu-177-PSMA (Pluvicto) in patients with progressive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial specifically looks at patients with moderate to severe kidney impairment compared to those with normal kidney function to understand dosing safety in this population.

items.title: Talazoparib With or Without Enzalutamide After Abiraterone in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether talazoparib (a PARP inhibitor) alone or combined with enzalutamide can delay cancer progression in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have DNA repair gene mutations and previously received abiraterone. The study focuses on patients with specific genetic vulnerabilities.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways in Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Development
items.summary: This research paper reviews how chronic inflammation drives prostate cancer progression to castration-resistant disease through activation of NFκB and JAK/STAT3 signaling pathways. The paper explains how inflammatory signals reshape the cancer's genetic landscape, promote tumor survival and spread, and contribute to treatment resistance. Understanding these mechanisms may reveal new therapeutic targets.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a next-generation DNA vaccine targeting PSMA (a prostate cancer protein) that can prevent tumor growth and lung metastases in animal models. The vaccine increased immune system activation and improved response to PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor immunotherapy, suggesting potential for combination approaches in aggressive disease.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes Resistance in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers designed a new drug that simultaneously blocks both BRD4 and AKT proteins to overcome resistance to AKT inhibitors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study found that targeting both pathways together can counter c-MYC-driven resistance that limits single-drug effectiveness. Compound 21d showed promising results in laboratory studies.

items.title: Effectiveness of Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This meta-analysis of 21 clinical trials involving 1,580 patients examined immune checkpoint inhibitor effectiveness in unselected metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients. Results showed modest benefits: 63% one-year survival and 41% six-month progression-free survival. Combination therapies with checkpoint inhibitors showed more promise than single or dual checkpoint inhibitor treatments alone.

items.title: Regulatory T Cells in Prostate Cancer Immune Evasion
items.summary: This review examines how regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the prostate tumor environment help cancer evade the immune system. Research shows that high Treg density in tumor tissue more than doubles the risk of cancer recurrence, and activated suppressive Tregs are more common in aggressive tumors. The paper discusses current and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting Tregs.

items.title: Bone Health Effects of Enzalutamide With or Without Zoledronic Acid
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studied bone health in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients receiving hormone therapy plus enzalutamide with or without zoledronic acid (a bone-protecting drug). After 18 months, patients receiving zoledronic acid had significantly better preservation of bone density at the femoral neck and lumbar spine compared to those without it, supporting bone protection strategies during treatment.
